_comment: R3 (MASTER-ROADMAP.md Step 9 / ledger QUAL-6) + Track C card C8 (2026-08-14), the editor+Python extension R3 explicitly deferred. Ratchet floor per module, read/written by scripts/quality/check-coverage-ratchet.py. A module NOT yet measured for real starts at coveragePercent 0.0 / measuredOn null so the FIRST real measurement sets the floor rather than blocking a merge -- never hand-edit a coveragePercent upward; let the ratchet script do it from a real report. A DROP below the recorded value for a module that produced a fresh report this run is a gate failure; a module with no fresh report this run is reported as not-measured, never failed. Each module now declares reportFormat (jacoco-xml / istanbul-json-summary / coverage-py-json) since the editor and Python tooling don't emit JaCoCo's XML shape -- see check-coverage-ratchet.py's module docstring for the three parsers.

NPDevContract/dsl.note: dsl has no settings.gradle of its own; it is built as a subproject of the root, NPDevGenerator, or NPDevKernel multi-project builds, so its jacoco report lands under whichever rootProject.name built it last (layout.buildDirectory is redirected to the external Build root -- see each build.gradle's resolveNpdevBuildRoot).

NPDevGenerator/generator.note: Produced by :generator:test (run-generator-gate.ps1's generatorQualityGate). local-only tests unless -PincludePackagedProofs or CI=1 -- see NPDevGenerator/generator/build.gradle's packaged-proof exclusion. Custom classloaders used by TrustedSourceEmitterGeneratedActionTest et al. compile+load throwaway classes outside src/main/java, so they are invisible to this report by construction, not a defect in the report.

NPDevKernel/kernel.note: Aggregate across :kernel and every :adapters:* subproject (36 of them), summed by check-coverage-ratchet.py from whichever per-subproject XML reports exist -- there is no dedicated CI gate that runs kernelQualityGate today (a pre-existing gap this card does not close), so this stays at the placeholder until someone runs it (locally: gradlew kernelQualityGate -PenableCoverage is not needed here, kernel never ships into a generated app).

NPDevRuntimeHost.note: Only produced when the assembled sample app is built with -PenableCoverage=true (run-runtimehost-gate.ps1 does this and copies the report to the stable path above before its own build-cache cleanup runs). JaCoCo does NOT ship inside generated FinalApps by default -- see NPDevRuntimeHost/build.gradle.template's own gating comment.

NPDevCli.note: Track C C8. run-ai-knowledge-gate.ps1 step [18/35] already ran `python -m unittest discover -s NPDevCli/tests` (REG-110) -- now wrapped in `coverage run --source=NPDevCli --omit=NPDevCli/tests/*,NPDevCli/tests/fixtures/*` and reported via `coverage json`, so this runs (and is measured) even in the standalone ai-knowledge-gate.yml CI job, unlike the Java/editor modules above which need a real build/npm run first. coverage.py's 'statement coverage' is the same conceptual LINE metric as JaCoCo's, just named differently. This floor is PLATFORM-DEPENDENT and was deliberately pinned from the Linux CI job's own measurement, not a local Windows dev machine's: NPDevCli has dozens of `os.name == "nt"` branches (npdev_cli.py, dev_loop.py, npdev_monitor.py, npdev_explore.py), so the same 145 tests cover a few more lines on Windows (30.2947%, 1768/5836) than on Linux (30.1576%, 1760/5836) -- committing the higher Windows number would have made every Linux CI run read as a permanent, unfixable regression. If this ever needs re-measuring by hand, prefer the CI job's own output over a local run on any OS. 2026-08-14 (reconciliation, merging all roadmap branches): re-measured to 30.1215% (1758/5836 -- 2 fewer covered lines than the original 30.1576% measurement) after merging main forward past this PR's own merge-base -- several sibling PRs (R9's --web-assets flag, R10's screen-mount work) added a handful of new NPDevCli lines with no matching test coverage in the interim. This is expected reconciliation drift, not a real test regression -- the underlying test suite is unchanged; re-pinned to the real current CI-measured number per this note's own guidance.

NPDevMcp.note: Track C C8 investigated this and found NPDevMcp/server.py has NO dedicated automated test suite anywhere in the repo (git ls-files under NPDevMcp turns up only server.py + README.md) -- not silently skipped, an honestly-labelled pre-existing gap of the same shape as the kernel entry above. This module stays at the 0.0/null placeholder until a future card adds real tests to run under coverage.py; the reportGlobs path is reserved so that first measurement has somewhere to land without another baseline-schema edit.

scripts.note: Track C C8 investigated this and found the ~150 scripts/**/*.py files (mostly the check-*.py quality-gate scripts) have no unittest/pytest suite of their own -- each instead carries its own ad-hoc `--calibrate` self-test mode (20 of them, see run_calibration()-shaped functions), a different testing paradigm not wired to coverage.py. A handful of scripts/ files DO get incidentally exercised by NPDevCli/tests (e.g. test_engines.py imports scripts/quality/check-config-schema.py directly), which is exactly why this is its OWN placeholder entry rather than folded into NPDevCli's --source: lumping ~150 largely-untested linter scripts into NPDevCli's denominator would dilute that module's real, meaningful floor into a near-frozen near-zero number. Stays at 0.0/null, an honestly-labelled pre-existing gap, until a future card gives scripts/ its own real test suite.
